plan_summary: Split implementation into 5-7 TypeScript files (types.ts, utils.ts, ToolPage.tsx, CommentsSection.tsx, badges.tsx, CodeBlock.tsx, VideoEmbed.tsx) following single-responsibility principle. Critical fix: formatRelativeTime uses threshold-based approach where diff >= 2592000000ms (30 days) transitions from 'Xd ago' to months via Math.floor(days/30), ensuring exactly 30 days yields '1 month ago'. Badges use inline styles for dynamic HexColor. Convex useQuery/useMutation for real-time comments. Type guard isToolSlug validates slug params. aspect-video Tailwind class for VideoEmbed with sandbox/referrerPolicy security attributes. All exports have explicit TypeScript type annotations. 21 types, 9 functions, targeting 49 contract tests.
efficiency_assessment: The plan is efficient and well-structured. File decomposition into 5-7 files is appropriate — it respects the 300-line limit while avoiding excessive fragmentation. Grouping StepBadge and VersionBadge into a single badges.tsx is sensible given their shared pattern (inline style for accentColor). The utility functions (formatRelativeTime, isToolSlug, buildToolMap) co-locate well in utils.ts since they are pure functions with no React dependencies, enabling straightforward unit testing without component rendering overhead. The O(1) lookup via buildToolMap (Record<ToolSlug, ToolDef>) is optimal for ToolPage route resolution. No unnecessary dependencies are introduced — no date-fns, no external clipboard libraries. The approach is implementation-minimal while covering all 9 functions and 21 types.
compliance_assessment: Fully compliant with project operating procedures and research findings: (1) TypeScript only — all files .ts/.tsx, no Python. (2) React 18 functional components with typed props interfaces. (3) Tailwind CSS v3 for styling, inline styles only where Tailwind cannot handle dynamic values (HexColor on badges). (4) React Router v6 useParams() for slug extraction. (5) Convex useQuery/useMutation from 'convex/react' for real-time comments. (6) Explicit return type annotations on all exports. (7) Files under 300 lines. (8) vitest-compatible pure function separation. (9) Security attributes on VideoEmbed iframe (sandbox, referrerPolicy, allow). (10) No class components, no custom CSS. All research-identified best practices are addressed.
risk_assessment: RISK 1 — formatRelativeTime boundary (HIGH, mitigated): The prior attempt FAILED on 'test_thirty_days_ago'. The plan correctly identifies the fix: use strict threshold comparison where days >= 30 transitions to month output. However, the exact comparison operator is critical. The plan must ensure: (a) diff is computed as Date.now() - createdAt in milliseconds, (b) seconds = Math.floor(diff / 1000), (c) days = Math.floor(seconds / 86400), (d) threshold check: if days >= 30, compute months = Math.floor(days / 30) and return `${months} month(s) ago`. Exactly 30 days (2592000000ms) → days = 30 → months = 1 → '1 month ago'. The risk is in the exact string format — the test may expect '1 month ago' vs '1 months ago' (pluralization). Plan should handle singular/plural: months === 1 ? '1 month ago' : `${months} months ago`. Same for years. RISK 2 — Test expectation format (MEDIUM): With 49 contract tests, exact string formats for all formatRelativeTime outputs must match expectations. 'just now' vs '0s ago', 'Xm ago' vs 'X minutes ago', etc. The research suggests shorthand ('Xm ago', 'Xh ago', 'Xd ago') but months use long form ('X months ago'). This mixed format could be a trap — need to verify. RISK 3 — Convex API shape (LOW): The plan assumes api.comments.getByTool and api.comments.add — these must align with the convex_schema dependency. If the Convex function names differ, tests will fail. RISK 4 — ToolSlug enum values (LOW): isToolSlug depends on knowing the valid slug values. These likely come from the shared_types dependency. If the enum is defined there, the plan is fine; if not, we must define them correctly. RISK 5 — Future timestamps / negative diff (LOW): Plan should clamp negative diffs to 0 and return 'just now'.
